note: English B2 listening in the Cambridge B2 First format (owner's plan 2026-10-30): Part 1 short extracts ×8 (en_talk), Part 2 sentence completion ×10 (en_fill, typed), Part 3 five speakers matched to eight statements (en_match), Part 4 an interview ×7 (en_q). Each recording twice in the mock. Original texts. Drafted in tools/.mockups/en_b2_ls.py.

lines.s: You hear a woman talking about a course she did.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位女士談她上過的課程。
lines.en: You hear a woman talking about a course she did.

lines.s: I'd assumed a photography course would be mostly about cameras and settings, and of course there was some of that. But what really stayed with me was how much time we spent just looking — at light, at shapes, at people. I see things differently now, even without a camera in my hand.
lines.zh: 我原本以為攝影課主要是講相機和設定，當然也有一些。但真正讓我印象深刻的，是我們花了很多時間只是「看」——看光線、形狀、人。現在就算手上沒有相機，我看東西的方式也不一樣了。
lines.en: I'd assumed a photography course would be mostly about cameras and settings, and of course there was some of that. But what really stayed with me was how much time we spent just looking — at light, at shapes, at people. I see things differently now, even without a camera in my hand.

ask.s: What does she say about the course?
ask.en: What does she say about the course?

options.t: It changed the way she notices things.
It focused too much on technical details.
It was mainly about photographing people.

explain.zh: 真正讓她印象深刻的是學會「看」，「現在看東西的方式也不一樣了」。
explain.en: It changed how she sees things.

lines.s: You hear two friends talking about a new café.
lines.zh: 你聽到兩個朋友談一家新咖啡店。
lines.en: You hear two friends talking about a new café.

lines.s: Have you tried the new café on King Street?
lines.zh: 你去過國王街那家新咖啡店嗎？
lines.en: Have you tried the new café on King Street?

lines.s: Twice. The coffee's nothing special, but it's the only place round here where you can actually find a quiet table to work at.
lines.zh: 去過兩次。咖啡沒什麼特別，可是那是附近唯一真的能找到安靜位子工作的地方。
lines.en: Twice. The coffee's nothing special, but it's the only place round here where you can actually find a quiet table to work at.

lines.s: That's exactly what I need.
lines.zh: 那正是我需要的。
lines.en: That's exactly what I need.

ask.s: What do they both like about the café?
ask.zh: 他們兩個都喜歡這家咖啡店的什麼？
ask.en: What do they both like about the café?

options.t: the quality of the coffee
the low prices
the chance to work there in peace

explain.zh: 咖啡沒什麼特別，但「能找到安靜位子工作」，男的說「那正是我需要的」。

lines.s: You hear a man talking about his job as a tour guide.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士談他當導遊的工作。
lines.en: You hear a man talking about his job as a tour guide.

lines.s: People think the difficult part is remembering all the history, but that's easy once you've done it a few times. What's hard is keeping a group of thirty tired tourists interested at four o'clock in the afternoon.
lines.zh: 大家以為最難的是記住所有歷史，其實帶過幾次就很簡單了。難的是在下午四點，讓一團三十個累壞的遊客保持興趣。
lines.en: People think the difficult part is remembering all the history, but that's easy once you've done it a few times. What's hard is keeping a group of thirty tired tourists interested at four o'clock in the afternoon.

ask.s: What does he find most challenging?
ask.zh: 他覺得最有挑戰的是什麼？
ask.en: What does he find most challenging?

options.t: learning historical facts
holding people's attention
organising large groups

explain.zh: 記歷史很簡單，難的是「讓累壞的遊客保持興趣」。

lines.s: You hear a student talking about choosing a university.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位學生談選大學。
lines.en: You hear a student talking about choosing a university.

lines.s: Everyone told me to choose the university with the best reputation. But when I visited, I just didn't feel comfortable there. The smaller one felt friendlier, and the course had more practical work, which is how I learn best. So that's where I'm going.
lines.zh: 大家都叫我選名氣最大的大學。可是我去參觀時，就是覺得不自在。比較小的那間感覺比較友善，課程也有比較多實作，那是我最好的學習方式。所以我要去那間。
lines.en: Everyone told me to choose the university with the best reputation. But when I visited, I just didn't feel comfortable there. The smaller one felt friendlier, and the course had more practical work, which is how I learn best. So that's where I'm going.

ask.s: Why did she choose the smaller university?
ask.zh: 她為什麼選比較小的大學？
ask.en: Why did she choose the smaller university?

options.t: Her friends were going there.
It had a better reputation.
The course suited her way of learning.

explain.zh: 「課程有比較多實作，那是我最好的學習方式」。
explain.en: More practical work suits how she learns.

lines.s: You hear a man leaving a voicemail for a colleague.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士給同事留語音訊息。
lines.en: You hear a man leaving a voicemail for a colleague.

lines.s: Hi Sarah, it's Mike. About tomorrow's presentation — I've finished the slides, but I'm not happy with the figures in section three. Could you check them before you send everything to the client? I don't want them to see any mistakes.
lines.zh: 莎拉，我是麥克。關於明天的簡報，投影片我做好了，但我對第三部分的數字不太放心。你寄給客戶之前可以幫我檢查一下嗎？我不想讓他們看到錯誤。
lines.en: Hi Sarah, it's Mike. About tomorrow's presentation — I've finished the slides, but I'm not happy with the figures in section three. Could you check them before you send everything to the client? I don't want them to see any mistakes.

ask.s: What does Mike want Sarah to do?
ask.en: What does Mike want Sarah to do?

options.t: check some information
finish the slides
contact the client today

explain.zh: 「你寄給客戶之前可以幫我檢查一下嗎」：檢查第三部分的數字。

lines.s: You hear a woman talking about moving to the countryside.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位女士談搬到鄉下。
lines.en: You hear a woman talking about moving to the countryside.

lines.s: I expected to miss the shops and restaurants, and I don't at all. What I hadn't expected was how dark it gets at night. In the city, there's always some light. Here, without a torch, you can't see your own hand.
lines.zh: 我以為自己會想念商店和餐廳，結果完全不會。我沒料到的是晚上會這麼暗。在城市裡總有一點光，這裡沒有手電筒，連自己的手都看不見。
lines.en: I expected to miss the shops and restaurants, and I don't at all. What I hadn't expected was how dark it gets at night. In the city, there's always some light. Here, without a torch, you can't see your own hand.

ask.s: What surprised her about living in the countryside?
ask.zh: 住在鄉下讓她意外的是什麼？
ask.en: What surprised her about living in the countryside?

options.t: how much she missed the city
how dark the nights are
how far it is to the shops

explain.zh: 「我沒料到的是晚上會這麼暗」；她並不想念商店。
explain.en: How dark it gets at night.

lines.s: You hear two colleagues talking about a meeting.
lines.zh: 你聽到兩位同事談一場會議。
lines.en: You hear two colleagues talking about a meeting.

lines.s: That meeting went on for two hours and we still didn't decide anything.
lines.zh: 那個會開了兩個小時，結果什麼都沒決定。
lines.en: That meeting went on for two hours and we still didn't decide anything.

lines.s: I know. Next time, we should send everyone the agenda the day before, so people come prepared.
lines.zh: 我知道。下次我們應該前一天把議程寄給大家，讓大家有準備再來。
lines.en: I know. Next time, we should send everyone the agenda the day before, so people come prepared.

ask.s: What does the man suggest?
ask.en: What does the man suggest?

options.t: having shorter meetings
inviting fewer people
giving people information in advance

explain.zh: 「前一天把議程寄給大家」：事先給資訊。
explain.en: Send the agenda the day before.

lines.s: You hear a man talking about learning to cook.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士談學做菜。
lines.en: You hear a man talking about learning to cook.

lines.s: I followed recipes exactly for years and never really understood why they worked. Then a friend told me to stop measuring everything and taste as I go. It sounds obvious, but it completely changed my cooking.
lines.zh: 我多年來都完全照食譜做，從來不懂為什麼這樣做會好吃。後來一個朋友叫我別再什麼都量，邊煮邊嚐。聽起來理所當然，卻徹底改變了我的廚藝。
lines.en: I followed recipes exactly for years and never really understood why they worked. Then a friend told me to stop measuring everything and taste as I go. It sounds obvious, but it completely changed my cooking.

ask.s: What helped him to cook better?
ask.zh: 什麼幫他把菜做得更好？
ask.en: What helped him to cook better?

options.t: tasting the food while cooking
following recipes carefully
taking a cookery course

explain.zh: 朋友叫他「邊煮邊嚐」，徹底改變了他的廚藝。

lines.s: Hello, I'm Dr Anna Kerr, and I study sleep. I'm often asked how much sleep people really need. For most adults, the answer is between seven and nine hours, although teenagers need more — around nine. One of the biggest problems today is light from screens. It tells the brain that it's still daytime, so it delays the release of melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy. My advice is to switch off phones at least an hour before bed. Temperature matters too: a bedroom should be cool, ideally around eighteen degrees. Many people believe that a glass of wine helps them sleep. In fact, alcohol reduces the quality of sleep in the second half of the night. And if you can't sleep, don't lie there worrying — get up, go to another room and read something until you feel tired. Finally, try to wake up at the same time every day, even at weekends. Your body clock will thank you.
lines.zh: 大家好，我是安娜·柯爾博士，研究睡眠。常有人問我，人到底需要睡多久。大多數成人是七到九小時，不過青少年需要更多，大約九小時。現在最大的問題之一是螢幕的光。它告訴大腦現在還是白天，所以會延遲褪黑激素的分泌，那是讓我們想睡的荷爾蒙。我的建議是睡前至少一小時關掉手機。溫度也很重要：臥室應該涼一點，最好大約十八度。很多人以為喝一杯酒有助睡眠，其實酒精會降低後半夜的睡眠品質。如果睡不著，不要躺著擔心——起床到另一個房間看點東西，直到覺得累。最後，試著每天在同一時間起床，週末也一樣，你的生理時鐘會感謝你。
lines.en: Hello, I'm Dr Anna Kerr, and I study sleep. I'm often asked how much sleep people really need. For most adults, the answer is between seven and nine hours, although teenagers need more — around nine. One of the biggest problems today is light from screens. It tells the brain that it's still daytime, so it delays the release of melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy. My advice is to switch off phones at least an hour before bed. Temperature matters too: a bedroom should be cool, ideally around eighteen degrees. Many people believe that a glass of wine helps them sleep. In fact, alcohol reduces the quality of sleep in the second half of the night. And if you can't sleep, don't lie there worrying — get up, go to another room and read something until you feel tired. Finally, try to wake up at the same time every day, even at weekends. Your body clock will thank you.

ask.en: Most adults need between seven and ＿＿＿＿＿ hours of sleep.

explain.zh: 「大多數成人是七到九小時」。

ask.en: Alcohol reduces sleep quality in the ＿＿＿＿＿ half of the night.

ask.en: If you can't sleep, go to another room and ＿＿＿＿＿ something.

explain.zh: 「到另一個房間看點東西」。

ask.en: Do this even at ＿＿＿＿＿.

lines.s: Speaker 1
lines.zh: 說話者 1
lines.en: Speaker 1

lines.s: I started playing the guitar at forty, which people find funny. My teacher said it would take years to sound decent, but within six months I was playing songs I'd loved since I was a teenager. I honestly couldn't believe it.
lines.zh: 我四十歲才開始彈吉他，大家覺得很好笑。老師說要好幾年才能彈得像樣，可是六個月內我就能彈從青少年時期就喜歡的歌。我真的不敢相信。
lines.en: I started playing the guitar at forty, which people find funny. My teacher said it would take years to sound decent, but within six months I was playing songs I'd loved since I was a teenager. I honestly couldn't believe it.

lines.s: Speaker 2
lines.zh: 說話者 2
lines.en: Speaker 2

lines.s: My grandfather was a carpenter, and he taught me to make furniture in his workshop when I was small. Now I build tables and chairs at the weekend. Every time I pick up his old tools, I think of him.
lines.zh: 我爺爺是木匠，我小時候他在工作室教我做家具。現在我週末會做桌椅。每次拿起他留下的舊工具，我都會想起他。
lines.en: My grandfather was a carpenter, and he taught me to make furniture in his workshop when I was small. Now I build tables and chairs at the weekend. Every time I pick up his old tools, I think of him.

lines.s: Speaker 3
lines.zh: 說話者 3
lines.en: Speaker 3

lines.s: I joined a running club after I moved to a new city and didn't know anyone. Now my closest friends are people I met there. We still run together twice a week, and we usually go for breakfast afterwards.
lines.zh: 我搬到新城市、誰都不認識，就加入了跑步社。現在我最好的朋友都是在那裡認識的。我們還是每週一起跑兩次，跑完通常一起吃早餐。
lines.en: I joined a running club after I moved to a new city and didn't know anyone. Now my closest friends are people I met there. We still run together twice a week, and we usually go for breakfast afterwards.

lines.s: Speaker 4
lines.zh: 說話者 4
lines.en: Speaker 4

lines.s: I took up painting because my job is so stressful. I'm not very good, and I don't really care. For two hours every Sunday, I forget about work completely. That's the whole point for me.
lines.zh: 我開始畫畫是因為工作壓力太大。我畫得不太好，也不怎麼在乎。每個星期天的兩個小時，我能完全忘掉工作。對我來說，重點就在這裡。
lines.en: I took up painting because my job is so stressful. I'm not very good, and I don't really care. For two hours every Sunday, I forget about work completely. That's the whole point for me.

lines.s: Speaker 5
lines.zh: 說話者 5
lines.en: Speaker 5

lines.s: I used to be terrified of speaking in public. Joining a theatre group was my sister's idea, and I hated the first few rehearsals. But being on stage has changed me. I'm much more confident at work now, too.
lines.zh: 我以前非常害怕在大家面前說話。參加劇團是我姊姊的主意，前幾次排練我很討厭。可是站上舞台改變了我，現在我在工作上也有自信多了。
lines.en: I used to be terrified of speaking in public. Joining a theatre group was my sister's idea, and I hated the first few rehearsals. But being on stage has changed me. I'm much more confident at work now, too.

lines.s: My guest today is Clara Webb, a wildlife filmmaker whose latest series follows wolves in Canada. Clara, how did you get into this kind of work?
lines.zh: 今天的來賓是野生動物紀錄片導演克拉拉·韋伯，她最新的影集記錄加拿大的狼。克拉拉，你怎麼會走進這一行？
lines.en: My guest today is Clara Webb, a wildlife filmmaker whose latest series follows wolves in Canada. Clara, how did you get into this kind of work?

lines.s: Completely by accident. I was studying biology and volunteered to help a film crew carry equipment for a week. I expected to be bored, but watching how they told a story with animals was fascinating. I changed my plans after that.
lines.zh: 完全是意外。我當時讀生物，自願幫一個攝影團隊搬一週的器材。我以為會很無聊，結果看他們怎麼用動物說故事，覺得非常迷人。從那之後我就改變了計畫。
lines.en: Completely by accident. I was studying biology and volunteered to help a film crew carry equipment for a week. I expected to be bored, but watching how they told a story with animals was fascinating. I changed my plans after that.

lines.s: Your new series took three years to film. Why so long?
lines.zh: 你的新影集拍了三年，為什麼這麼久？
lines.en: Your new series took three years to film. Why so long?

lines.s: Wolves are extremely shy, so for the first year we hardly saw them at all. We had to let them get used to our presence. People imagine the hard part is the cold, but it's really the patience.
lines.zh: 狼非常怕生，所以第一年我們幾乎看不到牠們。我們得讓牠們習慣我們的存在。大家以為最難的是寒冷，其實真正難的是耐心。
lines.en: Wolves are extremely shy, so for the first year we hardly saw them at all. We had to let them get used to our presence. People imagine the hard part is the cold, but it's really the patience.

lines.s: Some viewers have said the series makes wolves look too friendly. What's your response?
lines.zh: 有些觀眾說這部影集把狼拍得太友善了，你怎麼回應？
lines.en: Some viewers have said the series makes wolves look too friendly. What's your response?

lines.s: I understand the concern, but we never changed what happened. Wolves are often shown as monsters, and I wanted to show them as family animals, which they are. That doesn't mean they aren't dangerous.
lines.zh: 我理解這個擔心，但我們從沒改動實際發生的事。狼常被描繪成怪物，我想呈現牠們是重視家庭的動物，而牠們確實是。這不代表牠們不危險。
lines.en: I understand the concern, but we never changed what happened. Wolves are often shown as monsters, and I wanted to show them as family animals, which they are. That doesn't mean they aren't dangerous.

lines.s: What do you hope people take away from it?
lines.zh: 你希望觀眾從中得到什麼？
lines.en: What do you hope people take away from it?

lines.s: Mostly, I'd like them to question what they think they know. If one person watches it and decides to find out more, that's enough for me.
lines.zh: 我最希望大家質疑自己以為知道的事。只要有一個人看完後決定去多了解一些，對我來說就夠了。
lines.en: Mostly, I'd like them to question what they think they know. If one person watches it and decides to find out more, that's enough for me.

ask.s: How did Clara become a wildlife filmmaker?
ask.zh: 克拉拉怎麼成為野生動物紀錄片導演的？
ask.en: How did Clara become a wildlife filmmaker?

options.t: She studied filmmaking at university.
A short volunteer job changed her plans.
A biology teacher encouraged her.

explain.zh: 自願幫攝影團隊搬一週器材，「從那之後我就改變了計畫」。
explain.en: A week helping a film crew changed her plans.

ask.s: What did she expect before working with the film crew?
ask.zh: 和攝影團隊工作前，她預期會怎樣？
ask.en: What did she expect before working with the film crew?

options.t: that she would find it dull
that it would be dangerous
that she would learn a lot

explain.zh: 「我以為會很無聊」。

ask.s: Why did the series take three years to film?
ask.en: Why did the series take three years to film?

options.t: The weather was very bad.
The crew was very small.
The wolves needed time to accept the crew.

explain.zh: 狼很怕生，「我們得讓牠們習慣我們的存在」。
explain.en: The wolves had to get used to them.

ask.s: What does Clara say was the hardest part?
ask.zh: 克拉拉說最難的是什麼？
ask.en: What does Clara say was the hardest part?

options.t: the cold
being patient
carrying the equipment

explain.zh: 「大家以為最難的是寒冷，其實真正難的是耐心」。

ask.s: How does Clara respond to the criticism of the series?
ask.zh: 克拉拉怎麼回應對影集的批評？
ask.en: How does Clara respond to the criticism of the series?

options.t: She says the events were shown truthfully.
She admits she made the wolves look friendly.
She says wolves are not dangerous.

explain.zh: 「我們從沒改動實際發生的事」；她也說這不代表狼不危險。
explain.en: Nothing was changed; wolves can still be dangerous.

ask.s: How does Clara describe wolves?
ask.en: How does Clara describe wolves?

options.t: as monsters
as easy to film
as animals that care about their families

explain.zh: 「我想呈現牠們是重視家庭的動物，而牠們確實是」。

ask.s: What does Clara hope viewers will do?
ask.zh: 克拉拉希望觀眾怎麼做？
ask.en: What does Clara hope viewers will do?

options.t: visit Canada
think again about what they believe
support wildlife charities

explain.zh: 「我最希望大家質疑自己以為知道的事」。
explain.en: Question what they think they know.
